proposal.title: Work together through linked questions and human decisions
proposal.summary: Choose how this wiki becomes our shared workshop: questions name the work, AI assistants prepare evidence and options, and people decide the next step.

options.name: One long planning document
options.benefit: A single reading path explains the broad idea.
options.tradeoff: Assignments, changes and connected choices need extra tracking.

options.name: Linked question cards and review packages
options.benefit: Each job has an owner, evidence, connected questions and a review route.
options.tradeoff: Keep the records and published wiki in step as work changes.

options.name: Issues as the primary workspace
options.benefit: Discussion and assignments sit directly in GitHub.
options.tradeoff: Provide a separate reading map so newcomers can follow the whole system.

proposal.recommendation: Use the linked wiki as the reading and question map, GitHub issues for review conversations, and versioned repository records for evidence and history.
authorises: Use the question IDs, work labels, agent job sheets and review records for planning.
Prepare research and design alternatives in parallel, with clear file ownership and handovers.
later_reviews: Each technical design, spending commitment, site use and operating service receives its relevant review.
Repository protection settings and reviewer roles are checked during GitHub setup.
review_checks: Can a newcomer find a useful job and understand what to bring back?
Can a reviewer see the exact proposal, evidence, responsibilities and next action?
Do changed proposals return to review while earlier decisions remain traceable?
Does the proposal identify overlapping professional responsibilities, applicable practice and legal sources, and the comparison of differences, improvements and deficiencies?

proposal.title: Design a kiosk family around its weather and working conditions
proposal.scope_label: The physical design brief and comparison drawings
proposal.summary: Choose a design approach that makes the public equipment, its power and its maintenance fit the conditions it will face. The existing artwork starts the visual conversation; this package starts the physical design.

options.name: A freestanding outdoor kiosk
options.benefit: A visible public point can be placed where people gather and need information.
options.tradeoff: Resolve enclosure, heat, water, wind, anchoring, safe access and maintenance together.

options.name: A public interface supported by a weather-protected host
options.benefit: The public screen connects to computing and service equipment in an agreed protected space.
options.tradeoff: Agree access, host responsibilities, cabling, independent power and support when the host is closed.

options.name: A portable continuity kit
options.benefit: Crews can reach events, exercises and temporary gaps with a transportable unit.
options.tradeoff: Plan transport, safe setup, deployment conditions, storage and return.

proposal.recommendation: Develop coordinated designs for a sheltered arcade demonstrator, an operational outdoor public kiosk and a portable continuity kit. Compare freestanding and host-supported arrangements before choosing the outdoor build.
authorises: Write the exposure and service requirements for each form.
Prepare alternative layouts, compartments, access arrangements and a measured parts-and-energy plan.
later_reviews: Engineering review, prices and a build decision follow the comparison drawings.
A real site brings its own host, cultural, installation and operating agreements.
Measured weather, energy and communication performance supports a later field trial.
review_checks: Are operating conditions, protection through a severe event, storage and recovery conditions clearly described?
Can a person use and maintain the equipment comfortably and safely?
Do the drawings show water paths, heat management, power separation, access and mounting?
Does each claimed capability have a planned measurement or review?
Does the proposal identify overlapping professional responsibilities, applicable practice and legal sources, and the comparison of differences, improvements and deficiencies?

proposal.title: Build a complete everyday-to-disaster service demonstration
proposal.scope_label: The first software and service demonstration
proposal.summary: Choose the first connected jobs to demonstrate, so we can test the kiosk, information, people, messages and Aura learning as a working whole.

options.name: Public information and calendar first
options.benefit: Demonstrate reviewed notices, events, corrections and saved information.
options.tradeoff: Request handovers and personal learning join in a later demonstration.

options.name: Connected service demonstration
options.benefit: Demonstrate public information, bounded assistance, readiness records and Aura learning across several simulated locations.
options.tradeoff: Use clear sample records and test the different receiving, approval and failure states.

options.name: Prepare a field pilot alongside the software
options.benefit: Develop a real host and hardware trial while the service takes shape.
options.tradeoff: Coordinate people, equipment, site arrangements and resources earlier.

proposal.recommendation: Start with a connected service demonstration using sample records at three logical locations and a portable unit. Practise everyday work, lost connections and recovery, then prepare the measured hardware and field trials.
authorises: Demonstrate three everyday tasks: find checked events and transport information; find a local notice or service; use guided assistance or learning.
Demonstrate disaster information, service/resource readiness and request handover with honest source and receipt states.
Prepare a 24-hour disconnected software exercise and a nine-day scenario timeline, each labelled by its test method.
later_reviews: People responsible for real information and requests agree their service arrangements before public use.
Actual endurance, weather performance and pilot-site readiness are established through their own measurements and reviews.
review_checks: Can residents and visitors complete the everyday jobs without a personal account?
Does a changed or unresolved warning keep its source, time and meaning when a connection fails?
Can people see whether a request is saved, received, assigned or completed?
Does Aura offer relevant learning with a source, prerequisites and a human handover?
Can another steward restore the service and continue outstanding work?
Does the proposal identify overlapping professional responsibilities, applicable practice and legal sources, and the comparison of differences, improvements and deficiencies?
